title: Social Engineering
requirements: Apps must not pretend to be another app in order to trick users into performing actions they intended for the original, trusted app.

title: Play Console Requirements
requirements: Developers must complete all Play Console requirements, including any profiles linked to the developer account.

Developers must choose the correct account type, and those offering financial products or services (banking, loans, stock trading, investment funds, crypto software wallets or exchanges), health apps (such as medical or human subjects research apps), apps approved to use VpnService, or government apps must register as an Organization.

Developer account information must be accurate: legal name and address, D-U-N-S number for organizations, contact email and phone, the developer email and phone shown on Google Play where applicable, payment methods where applicable, and a linked Google payment profile.
Organization accounts must keep their details current and consistent with their Dun & Bradstreet profile.
Before submission, all app information and metadata must be provided accurately.
Before submission, the app's privacy policy must be uploaded and the Data safety section completed.

Before submission, developers must provide an active demo account, current login information and any other resources reviewers need (such as sign-in details or a QR code), and must not submit outdated sign-in details.
App package names must be registered in Play Console to meet Android developer verification requirements.

The app should give a stable, engaging and responsive experience, everything in it (including ad networks, analytics services and third-party SDKs) must comply with the Developer Program Policies, and apps whose audience includes children must comply with the Families policy.

A change of developer account ownership must use the official account owner transfer process, and accounts must not be bought, sold or leased or obtained through third-party marketplaces or other illegitimate means; moving a single app uses the app owner transfer process.

title: Hostile Downloaders
requirements: Apps must not contain code that downloads mobile unwanted software, either because there is reason to believe it was built to spread such software and it has downloaded it or can download and install apps, or because at least 5% of the apps it downloads (with a minimum of 500 observed downloads) are mobile unwanted software.

Major browsers and file-sharing apps escape hostile downloader classification only if they never drive downloads without user interaction and every software download is initiated by a consenting user.

title: Android Emoji Policy
requirements: Apps must support the latest Unicode Emoji on Android 12 and later, and apps with custom emoji implementations, including third-party libraries, must add full support within 4 months of a new Unicode Emoji release.
Apps with custom emoji implementations, including ones from third-party libraries, must fully support a new Unicode Emoji release on Android 12 or later within 4 months of its release.

title: Google Play's Target API Level Policy
requirements: New apps and app updates must target an Android API level within one year of the latest major Android release, or they cannot be submitted in Play Console.
Existing apps that are not updated must target an API level within two years of the latest major Android release to remain available to new users on devices running newer Android versions.

title: Permissions and APIs that Access Sensitive Information
requirements: Apps may request sensitive permissions and APIs only when needed for current features promoted in the Play listing, and must not use them for undisclosed, unimplemented or disallowed purposes.
Personal or sensitive data obtained through permissions or sensitive APIs must never be sold or shared to facilitate a sale.

Apps must request sensitive permissions in context, incrementally, so users understand why, and must obtain fresh affirmative consent before using the data for any purpose beyond what the user agreed to.
Data accessed through restricted permissions (dangerous, special, signature or otherwise designated) is personal and sensitive data and must meet all User Data policy requirements.

Apps must honor a user's refusal of a restricted permission without manipulating or forcing consent to non-critical permissions, and must make a reasonable effort to offer an alternative such as manual entry.
Apps must not use any permission in a way that violates the Malware policy, including elevated privilege abuse.

Dangerous permissions must be requested through a runtime prompt with a clear explanation, and special permissions such as SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW must be granted by sending users to the system settings page.

Apps targeting API 33+ may request READ_MEDIA_IMAGES or READ_MEDIA_VIDEO only when the system Photo Picker or similar alternatives cannot provide core functionality, and must submit a Play Console declaration explaining why.
Apps must not request device storage access on behalf of a third party for purposes unrelated to core functionality.

Apps targeting API 30+ may request MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE only when platform intents such as the Storage Access Framework are insufficient for core functionality, must submit a Play Console declaration, and must prompt users to enable All files access under Special app access.

Apps may declare or request Call Log permissions only while actively registered as the default Phone or Assistant handler, and SMS permissions only while actively registered as the default SMS or Assistant handler, and must stop using them as soon as they lose that status.
Apps without default SMS, Phone or Assistant handler capability must not list SMS or Call Log permissions in the manifest at all, including as placeholders.

SMS and Call Log data may be used, shared or transferred only for approved core functionality prominently documented in the app description, never for advertising, marketing or improving other services, and must not be derived through other permissions, APIs or third-party sources; a Play Console declaration is required.
Apps must not access location data once it is no longer needed for a current feature, and must never request location permissions solely for advertising or analytics.

Apps should request the minimum location scope (coarse over fine, foreground over background) that users would reasonably expect for the feature, and may use background location only for user-beneficial features tied to core functionality, with the background location declaration completed.

Apps with only foreground location access may use location from a foreground service only as a continuation of a user-initiated in-app action, ending immediately once that action's use case is complete.
Apps designed for children must not request device location and must follow the Families policy.

Apps targeting API 30+ may use QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES or equivalent broad-visibility methods only when the core user-facing function requires awareness of or interoperability with all installed apps, must use targeted package queries when those suffice, and must submit a Play Console declaration.
Installed app inventory data must be used only for the app's core functionality and must never be sold or shared for analytics or ads monetization.

The Accessibility API must not be used to change settings without permission, block disabling or uninstalling apps (except authorized parental control or enterprise management), work around platform security or privacy controls and notifications, or alter the UI deceptively.
The Accessibility API must not be used for remote call audio recording or to power apps that autonomously initiate, plan and execute actions or decisions.

Apps using the Accessibility API must document that use in the Play listing, complete the Play Console declaration with a demo video, and must use more narrowly scoped APIs where they achieve the same result.

Only apps whose core function directly supports people with disabilities may set isAccessibilityTool; other apps using the Accessibility API must not set it and must provide a prominent in-app disclosure and obtain affirmative consent.

Apps may request REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES only when their core function, prominently described in the listing and declared in Play Console, involves sending or receiving packages and user-initiated installation, such as browsing, attachment-capable messaging, file management, enterprise management, backup and restore, device migration or wearable and IoT companion apps.

REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES must not be used for self-updates, modifying the app, or installing APKs bundled in assets (except device management), and every installation must be initiated by the user; peer-to-peer sharing qualifies only if it is the app's primary purpose.

Body sensor data (BODY_SENSORS, BODY_SENSORS_BACKGROUND and granular health permissions) is personal and sensitive, must follow the User Data and Health apps policies, and may be requested only for approved user-benefiting uses such as fitness tracking, condition monitoring, approved research or wearable companion features, never for advertising, analytics or health-based profiling.
Apps targeting Android 16+ must use the granular android.permission.health.* permissions instead of BODY_SENSORS for APIs that previously required it.

Apps may request Health Connect permissions only for approved use cases (fitness and wellness, rewards, coaching, corporate wellness, medical care, health research, games) with features that benefit users' health, must request only the minimum data types needed, and must submit a Play Console declaration.

Health Connect must not be used in safety-critical systems, by headless apps without a visible icon, to sync data between incompatible devices or platforms, or in apps or services that solely target children.
Apps using Health Connect must protect the data against unauthorized access and comply with applicable laws such as HIPAA and GDPR, including any required agreements.

Health Connect data use should be limited to providing or improving user-visible features, transfer to third parties is allowed only with explicit consent or for security, legal or merger reasons, and the data must never be sold or used for advertising, data brokers, creditworthiness or lending, unapproved medical devices, or non-compliant PHI handling.

Apps using Health Connect must publish a privacy policy that identifies the app, describes the data types accessed and all uses and sharing, explains how users manage and delete data and what happens on account deactivation or deletion, and describes secure handling.

Apps may use VpnService only if VPN is their core function or a remote server is needed for core functions such as parental control, enterprise management, app usage tracking, device security, network tools, browsers or carrier services.

Apps using VpnService must document it in the Play listing, encrypt traffic from device to tunnel endpoint, must not collect personal data without prominent disclosure and consent, and must not redirect or manipulate other apps' traffic for monetization.

Apps may declare USE_EXACT_ALARM (API 33+) only if their core user-facing function is an alarm, timer or calendar with event notifications; other apps needing exact alarms should use the user-granted SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM.

Apps targeting API 34+ receive USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT automatically only if their core function is alarms or receiving phone or video calls; other apps must ask the user for the permission with a clear explanation.

Full-screen intent notifications must be limited to high-priority alerts, must not interfere with or disrupt the device or be used for disruptive ads or notifications, and should not interfere with other apps.

Data from the Age Signals API may be used only to meet legal obligations such as providing age-appropriate experiences, never for advertising, marketing, personalization, analytics, profiling or transfer to third parties unless legally required.

announced.text: Apps targeting API 37+ must use the Android location button for one-time or infrequent location needs, and apps requesting ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION must submit a Play Console declaration explaining why coarse location or the location button is insufficient.
Apps that do not need broad contacts access for core functionality must use the Android Contact Picker instead of broad contacts permissions.
Apps exposing AppFunctions must not use them to deceive or manipulate AI agents, bypass security controls or interfere with other apps.

The Manage Contacts permission is limited to core functionality where system pickers are insufficient; apps targeting API 38+ need a Play Console declaration and all other apps must use narrowly scoped platform intents.
The Local Network permission is limited to core functionality where device pickers are insufficient, and apps targeting API 37+ must submit a Play Console declaration to use it.

title: Families Self-Certified Ads SDK Policy
requirements: Ads SDKs and mediation platforms that serve apps in the Families program must make ad content accessible to children appropriate for children, define and prohibit objectionable ad content and behavior in their terms or policies, and rate creatives into age groups that include at least Everyone and Mature using Google's methodology.

Ads SDKs serving children must ensure creatives delivered through real-time bidding have been reviewed against these rules, and must visually identify creatives from their inventory, for example with a watermark logo.
Ads SDKs must ensure that ads shown to children follow the Families ad format rules and must let developers choose compliant ad formats.

Ads shown to children must not be deceptive or cause accidental clicks (such as a dismiss button that opens another ad or ads appearing where users usually tap), must not be full-screen or interfering without a clear way to dismiss (such as ad walls), must be closeable after 5 seconds if they interrupt normal use (including rewarded or opt-in ads), must not have multiple placements on a page, must be clearly distinguishable from content (no unidentifiable offerwalls or immersive ads), and must not use shocking or emotionally manipulative tactics.
Ads SDKs must ensure ads shown to children involve no interest-based advertising or remarketing.

Ads SDKs must disclose their access, collection, use and sharing of data, limit use to the disclosed purposes, and disclose any collection of personal and sensitive information from children such as authentication data, microphone and camera data, device data, Android ID and ad usage data.

Ads SDKs must let developers request child-directed treatment per request or per app, compliant with laws such as COPPA and GDPR, and that treatment must disable personalized ads, interest-based advertising and remarketing.
Ads SDKs must propagate privacy indicators to bidders when real-time bidding serves ads to children.
Ads SDKs must not transmit AAID, SIM serial, build serial, BSSID, MAC, SSID, IMEI or IMSI from children or users of unknown age.

Mediation platforms serving ads to children must use only Families self-certified ads SDKs or safeguards that keep all mediated ads compliant, and must pass the ad content rating and any child-directed treatment to the mediated networks.

Self-certified ads SDKs must give Google enough information to verify compliance, including English versions of their terms of service, privacy policy and publisher integration guide and a fully built phone APK test app using the latest SDK version with all features, full live inventory access and no geolocation restriction, able to distinguish child-suitable from full inventory for mixed audiences.

Self-certified ads SDKs must certify every new version release against current Play policies including Families requirements, and must support ad serving that complies with COPPA, GDPR and other laws on children that apply to their publishers.

title: SDK Requirements
requirements: Developers are responsible for ensuring that every SDK in their app, and the SDK provider's handling of data from the app, complies with Play policy, and must know which permissions each SDK uses, what data it collects and why.

Data collected by SDKs must be limited to the app's disclosed, policy-compliant purposes that users would reasonably expect; for example an SDK that claims to collect data only for anti-fraud must not also share it for advertising or analytics.
SDK providers must not sell personal and sensitive user data from the app, whether the data is transferred from a server or through embedded code.
SDKs must handle personal and sensitive data securely, transmitting it with modern cryptography such as HTTPS, and must rely on runtime permission requests before accessing permission-gated data.

Data access or collection by an SDK that falls outside users' reasonable expectations, including SDKs that collect personal data by default, must meet the prominent disclosure and consent requirements, and the developer must be able to prove compliance within two weeks of a Google request.
Apps must not include SDKs that transmit the list of installed packages without meeting the prominent disclosure and privacy policy requirements.

SDKs must not link persistent device identifiers such as IMEI to other personal and sensitive data (such as location) or to resettable identifiers, must not connect the AAID to persistent identifiers for advertising or analytics, and must not connect the AAID to email addresses for analytics, outside the disclosed telephony and enterprise device owner exceptions.
Apps that target children may include only SDKs self-certified for child-directed services.
The Data safety section must accurately cover data collected and handled by all third-party libraries and SDKs in the app.

SDKs must not request sensitive permissions for undisclosed, unimplemented or disallowed purposes, such as background location for an undisclosed purpose or transmitting IMEI from READ_PHONE_STATE without consent.

Apps must not include SDKs that are malicious or come from providers that distribute malware, or that steal credentials, abuse elevated privileges or undisclosed device data access, prevent uninstallation, disable SELinux, root devices without permission, or commit carrier billing fraud.
Apps must not include SDKs that transmit audio or call recording data unrelated to compliant functionality, or that send data off the device unexpectedly or without adequate notice and consent.

Apps must not include SDKs that download executable code such as dex or native code from outside Google Play, update their own APK, download or install apps from unknown sources, or load runtime interpreted code that enables policy violations.
Apps must not include SDKs that load untrusted or unverified URLs into a WebView with an added JavaScript interface, or that download files over insecure connections.
SDKs may provide proxy services to third parties only when proxying is the app's primary user-facing purpose.
SDKs may use foreground services only for an appropriate use case, and those services must be declared in the app's manifest.
Apps must not include SDKs with hidden, dormant or undocumented features or with techniques to evade app review.

Apps must accurately describe their functionality, including SDK-provided functionality, in the description, images and video of all metadata, must not mimic OS or other apps' warnings, and must make device setting changes only with the user's knowledge and consent and in a reversible way.

title: Blockchain-based Content
requirements: Apps offering purchase, holding or exchange of cryptocurrency should do so through certified services in regulated jurisdictions, must comply with the regulations of every targeted region, and must not be published where those products or services are prohibited.
Apps must not mine cryptocurrency on the device, although apps that remotely manage mining are allowed.
Apps that sell tokenized digital assets or let users earn them must declare this in the Play Console Financial features declaration.
In-app products that represent tokenized digital assets must be marked as such in their product details.
Apps with tokenized digital assets must not promote or glamorize potential earnings from playing or trading.
Gambling apps that integrate tokenized digital assets such as NFTs should complete the gambling app application process.

Apps that are not approved gambling apps or pilots should not accept anything of monetary value for a chance to obtain an NFT of unknown value, and must disclose the specific contents and values when selling NFT bundles.
NFTs bought by users in games should be consumed or used in the game to enhance the experience or help users progress.
Apps must not let users wager or stake NFTs for a chance to win prizes of real-world monetary value, including other NFTs, for example pay-to-play social casino games that reward NFTs.

title: AI-Generated Content
requirements: Apps that generate content with generative AI from user prompts, such as chatbots central to the app or AI image and video generators, must comply with all Play policies and must prohibit and prevent generation of Restricted Content, such as content that facilitates child exploitation or abuse, and content that enables deceptive behavior.
Apps that generate content with AI must offer in-app reporting or flagging so users can report offensive content to the developer without leaving the app.
Developers of AI content generation apps should use user reports to inform the app's content filtering and moderation.

title: Age-Restricted Content and Functionality
requirements: Apps that facilitate real-money gambling, games or contests must use the Play Console tools to block minors.

Apps whose core function is matchmaking or dating must use the Play Console tools to block minors, while apps where dating or matchmaking is only an incidental feature must instead age-gate those features against minors.
Apps whose core function is randomly connecting users to communicate spontaneously with strangers must use the Play Console tools to block minors.
Apps whose core function is anonymous communication, where one or more users' identities are deliberately hidden, must use the Play Console tools to block minors.

title: Developer Program Policy
requirements: Apps must comply with the consolidated Developer Program Policy as in force since October 29, 2026 (unless a section states otherwise); its substantive rules are the same as the standalone policy pages, which are digested individually, so this entry only records the version and effective date.
Online Crane Game apps may be listed on Google Play globally only subject to applicable law and the additional conditions of the real-money gaming rules.

title: Policy announcement: October 29, 2026
requirements: Developers and apps must not engage in any behavior that manipulates the Play app review process.
Apps using the All Files Access permission (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) must limit use to the minimum scope their core functionality needs.
Apps using the Accessibility API must set the isAccessibilityTool flag and make the disclosures that correspond to their designation as an accessibility tool or not.

Cryptocurrency apps offered in Hong Kong must hold the applicable local license, which now includes the Virtual Asset Trading Platform license, unless they qualify for a local regulatory exemption under the Additional Options section.

Government or authorized mobile network operator apps may use READ_CALL_LOG for Quality of Service reporting; apps relying on the backup and restore exception for SMS or call log permissions must be able to restore data to the device's default handler.
Apps that facilitate purchases of digital goods or services through AI or agentic experiences are subject to the Payments policy.
Developers must declare their trader status in Play Console under the Console requirements in effect from November 2026.
Apps for XR headsets, wired XR glasses, or audio and display glasses should follow the updated Android XR app quality guidelines for immersive and augmented experiences.

announced.text: Developers who sell into or out of Japan must complete the payments authorization form, or their payments will be held globally.

Apps that offer subscriptions with ongoing eligibility-based discounts (for example student plans) must clearly disclose the eligibility criteria, the verification process, and how price and benefits change once eligibility ends.

Apps must request only the minimum location scope their core functionality needs; apps targeting API 37+ must use the Android location button for one-time or infrequent location requests, and apps using ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION must file a Play Console declaration explaining why coarse location or the location button is insufficient.
Account verification by phone call is no longer a permitted use of READ_CALL_LOG; apps must use an alternative such as the SMS User Consent API.
Apps must meet the new app quality requirements on memory and code optimization thresholds to keep visibility and publishing capabilities.
Apps that implement AppFunctions must comply with all Play policies, and their AppFunctions must not deceive or manipulate AI agents, bypass security controls, or interfere with other apps.
The Local Network permission is limited to apps whose core functionality needs it where device pickers are insufficient, and apps targeting API 37+ must file a Play Console declaration to use it.

The Manage Contacts permission is limited to apps whose core functionality needs it where system pickers are insufficient and requires a Play Console declaration; all other apps must use narrowly scoped platform intents.

title: Ads
requirements: Ads and their associated offers are part of the app and must follow all Play policies, including the Restricted Content policies, with additional rules for gambling apps.

Ads and the offers they promote (such as downloading another app) must be appropriate for the app's own content rating, for example no Teen or Mature ads or Mature app promotions in an app rated Everyone.
Apps that target children must follow the Families Ads and Monetization requirements for all ads.

Ads must not simulate or impersonate app UI elements or OS notifications and warnings, and it must be clear which app is serving each ad; features that look like app functions but only lead to ads are not allowed.
Apps must not force users to click an ad or submit personal information for advertising purposes before they can fully use the app.

Ads may be shown only inside the app serving them and must not interfere with other apps, other ads or device operation (including system buttons and ports), whether through overlays, companion functionality or widget ad units; ads must not appear on the home screen or be triggered by the home button or other exit actions.
Ads that take over the screen or interfere with normal use must be easily dismissible without penalty, and must not use false dismiss buttons or appear suddenly where users usually tap.

Full-screen interstitial ads of any format must not appear unexpectedly when the user has chosen to do something else, at the start of a game level or content segment, or (for video interstitials) before the splash screen.

Full-screen interstitial ads must be closeable after 15 seconds, except opt-in or non-interrupting interstitials (such as after a score screen); user opt-in rewarded ads and ads that do not interfere with normal use (such as integrated video ads or non-full-screen banners) are exempt from these interstitial rules.
Apps must not show interstitial ads repeatedly after consecutive user actions such as clicks or swipes in a way that distracts users from using the app.
Apps whose exclusive purpose is not being a lockscreen must not add ads or features that monetize the device's locked display.
Apps must not commit ad fraud.

Apps that use permission-based location data for ads must make that use clear to users and document it in the privacy policy with links to the relevant ad network privacy policies, and must never request location permissions solely for ads.
Apps may use the Android advertising ID only for advertising and user analytics, and must check the user's ads personalization opt-out setting each time they access it.

For advertising, the advertising ID must not be connected to persistent device identifiers such as SSAID, MAC or IMEI and may be connected to personally identifiable information only with the user's explicit consent; for analytics, it must not be connected to personally identifiable information or any persistent device identifier at all.
A reset or deleted advertising ID must not be connected to a previous advertising ID or data derived from it without the user's explicit consent.

When the user has opted out of ads personalization, apps must not use the advertising ID to build advertising profiles or target personalized ads, though contextual ads, frequency capping, conversion tracking, reporting and fraud detection remain allowed.

Apps must disclose collection and use of the advertising ID and their commitment to these terms in a legally adequate privacy notice, and any party they share it with must use it in line with Play policy.
Apps must use the advertising ID, when available on the device, instead of any other device identifier for advertising purposes.

title: Payments
requirements: Apps that charge for downloads from Google Play must use Google Play's billing system for those charges.

Apps that require or accept payment for in-app features, services, digital content or goods, such as virtual currency, extra lives, characters, content subscriptions, ad-free versions, premium features or cloud software and services, must use Google Play's billing system unless one of the policy's listed exceptions or enrolled programs applies.

Apps must not use Google Play's billing system for payments primarily for physical goods or physical services, credit card or utility bill remittances, peer-to-peer payments, online auctions, tax-exempt donations, online gambling, or product categories unacceptable under Google's Payments Center content policies.

Apps must not lead users to payment methods other than Google Play billing through their store listing, in-app promotions, WebViews, buttons, links, messages, ads or other calls to action, or through UI flows such as account creation or sign-up, except under the policy's exceptions or enrolled alternative billing or external offer programs.
In-app virtual currency must be usable only within the app or game title in which it was purchased.
Apps must clearly and accurately tell users the terms and pricing of the app and of any in-app features or subscriptions, and in-app prices must match the prices shown in the Play billing interface.
If the Play description mentions features that require a specific or additional charge, the listing must clearly state that payment is needed to access them.
Apps offering randomized virtual items from a purchase, such as loot boxes, must clearly disclose the odds of receiving each item before and close in time to the purchase.

Apps may offer an alternative in-app billing system, or lead users outside the app to purchase, only for users in eligible countries or regions and only after enrolling in the applicable program and meeting its terms and requirements.

title: Financial Services
requirements: Apps must not expose users to deceptive or harmful financial products or services, meaning products related to managing or investing money or cryptocurrency, including personalized advice.
Apps that contain or promote financial products or services must comply with the regulations of every region they target, including any locally required disclosures.
Any app with financial features must complete the Financial features declaration in Play Console.
Apps must not let users trade binary options.

Apps that provide personal loans (nonrecurring consumer loans such as payday, peer-to-peer or title loans, not mortgages, car loans or revolving credit), whether lending directly, generating leads or connecting consumers to third-party lenders, must set the app category to Finance and disclose in the app metadata the minimum and maximum repayment period, the maximum APR, and a representative example of the total loan cost including principal and all fees.

Personal loan and Earned Wage Access apps must have a privacy policy that comprehensively discloses access, collection, use and sharing of personal and sensitive data within this policy's restrictions.
Apps must not promote personal loans that require full repayment within 60 days or less of the loan being issued.

Apps that provide Earned Wage Access, whether directly, as lead generators or by connecting users to providers, must set the app category to Finance and disclose in the app metadata the repayment terms, all fees (including subscription and transaction fees) and a representative example of the total cost including all fees.

Personal loan apps, loan or credit line facilitation apps, accessory loan or credit apps (such as calculators and guides) and Earned Wage Access apps must not access sensitive data such as photos and contacts, and must not request READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO, READ_CONTACTS, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, READ_PHONE_NUMBERS or QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES.

Developers of financial apps must be properly licensed in every region where the app is available, and the licenses or documents proving their ability to provide the financial products must be linkable to the developer account.

Personal loan apps targeting the United States, including lead generators and lender connectors, must not offer loans with an APR of 36% or higher and must display the maximum APR calculated consistently with the Truth in Lending Act.

Personal loan apps targeting India must be on the RBI list of digital lending apps deployed by regulated entities and submit a license; platforms that only facilitate lending by registered NBFCs or banks must say so in the declaration and prominently list all partner NBFCs and banks in the app description.
Apps providing IT-based money lending services in Indonesia under OJK Regulation No. 77/POJK.01/2016 must submit a copy of their valid license.

Financing and lending companies offering loans through online lending platforms in the Philippines must hold a PSEC registration number and Certificate of Authority and disclose their corporate name, business name, PSEC registration number and Certificate of Authority in the app description, and lending-based crowdfunding apps such as P2P lending must process transactions through PSEC-registered crowdfunding intermediaries.

Digital money lenders in Nigeria must comply with the FCCPC digital lending framework and hold a verifiable FCCPC approval letter, and loan aggregators must provide documentation for their lending services and contact details for every partner lender.

Digital credit providers in Kenya must hold a Central Bank of Kenya license listed in the CBK Directory of Digital Credit Providers and submit it with the declaration, and facilitating platforms must say so and provide their partners' licenses.

In Pakistan each NBFC lender may publish only one digital lending app, developers must submit SECP approval to offer or facilitate digital lending, and short-term loan apps are not allowed except where explicitly permitted by Pakistani law.
Personal loan apps targeting Thailand with interest rates of 15% or more must hold a Bank of Thailand or Ministry of Finance license and provide it as documentation.

All personal loan apps targeting Thailand must show in the Play listing the BoT- or FPO-licensed loan provider names, the developer's legal entity name, and the maximum interest rates and all fees, and those with rates below 15% must also state that they are a non-regulated loan provider under the BoT/FPO.
Earned Wage Access apps must meet the country-specific loan requirements to the extent they apply in the relevant jurisdiction.

title: User Generated Content
requirements: Apps that contain or feature user-generated content, including specialized browsers or clients for UGC platforms, must require users to accept the terms of use or user policy before they can create or upload UGC.
UGC apps must define objectionable content and behavior consistently with Play policies and prohibit it in their terms of use or user policies.

UGC apps must carry out ongoing moderation appropriate to the type of content, including an in-app system to report and block objectionable content and users and action against offending content or users, and must address user complaints about objectionable content.
UGC apps limited to a verified or registered set of users (such as a school or company) must provide in-app reporting of content and users.
UGC features enabling 1:1 interaction with specific users, such as direct messages, tagging or mentions, must provide in-app user blocking.
Apps providing access to publicly accessible UGC, such as social networks and blogging apps, must provide in-app reporting of users and content and in-app user blocking.
Augmented reality apps with UGC must moderate, and let users report, both objectionable AR content and sensitive anchoring locations such as restricted areas or private property.
UGC apps must have safeguards so in-app monetization does not encourage objectionable behavior, for example no paid features that mainly encourage sharing objectionable content.
UGC apps must have sufficient safeguards against threats, harassment and bullying, particularly toward minors, including content intended to single out someone for abuse or ridicule.

UGC apps may contain only incidental sexual content (in apps that mainly offer non-sexual content and do not promote or recommend sexual content), and illegal sexual content or child endangerment content is never permitted.

UGC apps with incidental sexual content must hide it by default behind filters that take at least two user actions to fully disable, must block children from the app with an age screening system such as a neutral age screen, and must answer the UGC questions in the content rating questionnaire accurately.
Apps must not have the primary purpose of featuring objectionable UGC, and must not end up used primarily for hosting it or become known as a place where it thrives.

title: Real-Money Gambling, Games, and Contests
requirements: Apps that enable or facilitate online gambling are allowed only in select countries and only if the developer completes Google Play's gambling app application, is an approved governmental operator or licensed with the relevant gambling authority, and holds a valid license for each country or state where the app is distributed.

Gambling apps may offer only online casino games, sports betting, separately licensed horse racing, lotteries or daily fantasy sports, and must not offer any product beyond the scope of their license.
Gambling apps must comply with the laws and industry standards of every country where they are distributed.
Gambling apps must prevent under-age users from using the app and block access from any country, state or area not covered by the developer's license.
Gambling apps and daily fantasy sports apps must be free to download, must not be sold as paid apps, and must not use Google Play In-app Billing.
Gambling apps and daily fantasy sports apps must be rated AO (Adults Only) or the IARC equivalent.
Gambling apps and daily fantasy sports apps must clearly display responsible gambling information in the app and in the store listing.

Apps that are not approved gambling apps or approved pilots must not let users wager, stake or participate with real money or purchased in-app items for prizes of real-world monetary value, other than programs permitted under the gamified loyalty rules, including games that award cash or physical prizes for money, apps that accept or manage wagers, deposits or winnings, and navigation or calls to action (such as BET, REGISTER or COMPETE buttons or WebViews) inviting real-money contests.

Apps with gamified loyalty programs offering real-world prizes must make rewards clearly supplementary to a genuine, separate purchase of goods or services, with no part of the purchase acting as a participation fee or wager and no inflated price, and rewards must not be purchasable.

In game apps, loyalty rewards tied to purchases must be earned and redeemed only at a fixed ratio documented conspicuously in the app and in public official rules, and must not be wagered, multiplied or awarded based on game performance or chance.

Non-game apps with loyalty programs tied to purchases must publish official rules in the app, disclose the odds (for fixed-odds rewards) or the selection method (for other chance-based rewards), specify a fixed number of winners, entry deadline and award date for drawings or sweepstakes, and document any fixed accrual and redemption ratio conspicuously in the app and the rules.

Apps may show ads for gambling or real-money games, contests or tournaments only if the app and ads comply with local laws and ad licensing requirements, the app does not show such ads to known minors, is not in the Designed for Families program and does not target under-18s, and ads for gambling apps show responsible gambling information on the landing page, listing or in the app.

Apps showing gambling or real-money game ads (other than accepted gambling or DFS apps meeting the base ad requirements) must not offer simulated gambling such as social casino or virtual slots, must not provide companion functionality for wagering, payouts, odds or score tracking or fund management, and must not promote or direct users to gambling services; gambling ads must also not be disguised as buttons, icons or other interactive elements.

Daily fantasy sports apps are allowed only if distributed solely in the United States or approved through the gambling app process elsewhere, and only after the developer's DFS application is accepted.

Daily fantasy sports apps must comply with laws in every country, US state or territory where distributed, prevent under-age users from wagering or transacting, hold a valid license in every US state or territory that requires one, and block use from states or territories where the developer lacks a required license or DFS is illegal.
Online crane game apps and apps in real-money game pilots must follow the separate requirements published for them.

title: Child Endangerment
requirements: Apps must prohibit users from creating, uploading or distributing content that facilitates the exploitation or abuse of children, including any child sexual abuse material.

Apps must not be used to endanger children or promote predatory behavior toward them, including inappropriate interaction targeted at a child, grooming, sexualization of minors, sextortion or child trafficking.
Apps that appeal to children must not contain adult themes, such as excessive violence, blood and gore or depictions or encouragement of harmful and dangerous activities.
Apps must not promote negative body or self image, for example by depicting plastic surgery, weight loss or other cosmetic changes to appearance for entertainment.
Anonymous chat, random chat, social and dating apps must explicitly prohibit child sexual abuse and exploitation in publicly accessible standards such as terms of service or community guidelines.
Anonymous chat, random chat, social and dating apps must self-certify that they provide an in-app way for users to submit feedback, concerns or reports.

Anonymous chat, random chat, social and dating apps must self-certify that they take appropriate action, including removal, on CSAM once they have actual knowledge of it, and that they comply with child safety laws, including a process to report confirmed CSAM to NCMEC or the relevant regional authority.

Anonymous chat, random chat, social and dating apps must designate a child safety point of contact able to receive Google notices about CSAE content, speak to the app's enforcement and review procedures, and take action.

title: Inappropriate Content
requirements: Apps must not contain or promote sexual content or profanity, including pornography, depictions of sexual nudity, sex acts or sexually suggestive poses, sexual aids or sex guides, illegal sexual themes, fetishes or bestiality, or content intended to be sexually gratifying.
Apps and their store listings must not contain lewd or profane content such as profanity, slurs, explicit text or adult or sexual keywords.

Apps may contain nudity only when the primary purpose is educational, documentary, scientific or artistic and the nudity is not gratuitous; content allowed only in certain regions may make the app available only there.
Apps must not promote or solicit sexual acts for compensation, including sex-related entertainment, escort services or compensated dating arrangements such as sugar dating.

Apps must not contain content associated with sexually predatory behavior or distribute non-consensual sexual content, including creepshots, hidden camera content, deepfake sexual content or assault content, and must not degrade or objectify people, for example by claiming to undress people or see through clothing, even as a prank.

Catalog apps offering books, audiobooks or videos may include titles with sexual content only if such titles are a minor fraction of the catalog, are not actively promoted (beyond history-based recommendations or general price promotions), exclude child endangerment, porn and illegal sexual content, and are access-restricted for minors.

Apps must not promote violence or incite hatred against individuals or groups based on race, ethnicity, religion, disability, age, nationality, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, caste, immigration status or other characteristics tied to systemic discrimination, including claims that a protected group is inferior, inhuman, evil or a threat, hateful slurs or stereotypes, encouraging discrimination, or promoting hate symbols.

Apps must not depict or facilitate gratuitous violence or dangerous activities, such as graphic realistic violence or violent threats against people or animals, or promotion of self-harm, suicide, eating disorders, choking games or other acts that can cause serious injury or death; fictional game violence such as cartoons, hunting or fishing is generally allowed.
Terrorist or other dangerous organizations that have committed, prepared or claimed violence against civilians must not publish apps for any purpose, including recruitment.

Apps must not contain content related to violent extremism or to planning, preparing or glorifying violence against civilians, and any extremism-related content with educational, documentary, scientific or artistic purpose must include relevant context.

Apps must not capitalize on or be insensitive toward sensitive events such as emergencies, disasters, conflicts or deaths, including insensitivity about real deaths, denying well-documented tragedies, or appearing to profit without benefit to victims; content with educational, documentary, scientific or artistic value or awareness intent is generally allowed.

Apps must not contain or facilitate threats, harassment or bullying, including bullying conflict victims, extortion or blackmail, public humiliation, or harassing victims of tragedies and their families.

Apps must not facilitate the sale of explosives, firearms, ammunition or restricted firearm accessories, such as those that enable or simulate automatic fire (bump stocks, gatling triggers, auto sears, conversion kits) or magazines or belts holding more than 30 rounds.

Apps must not provide instructions for making explosives, firearms, ammunition, restricted firearm accessories or other weapons, including converting firearms to automatic or simulated automatic fire.

Apps must not facilitate the sale of marijuana or marijuana products regardless of legality, including in-app ordering, arranging delivery or pickup, or selling THC-containing products such as CBD oils with THC.

Apps must not facilitate the sale of tobacco or nicotine products such as e-cigarettes, vape pens and nicotine pouches, or advertise, promote or prominently feature tobacco products including links to tobacco sellers; limited tobacco sales in food or grocery delivery apps in certain regions and sales of nicotine cessation aids may be allowed only with age-gating safeguards.

Apps must not encourage illegal or inappropriate use of alcohol, tobacco or nicotine, including depicting or encouraging use or sale to minors, implying tobacco improves social, sexual, professional, intellectual or athletic standing, or portraying excessive, binge or competitive drinking favorably, and apps selling alcohol should use age-gating safeguards.

title: Illegal Activities
requirements: Apps must not facilitate or promote illegal activities, including facilitating the sale or purchase of illegal drugs or providing instructions for growing or manufacturing them.
Apps must not depict or encourage the use or sale of drugs, alcohol or tobacco by minors.

title: Health Content and Services
requirements: Apps that contain or promote health content or services must not expose users to harmful health content or services and must comply with applicable laws and regulations.
Apps that offer health-related features or information, or access health data for non-health features, must complete the Health apps declaration on the Play Console App content page.
Health apps must provide a privacy policy link in the Play Console field and a link or text inside the app, hosted on an active, public, non-geofenced, non-PDF and non-editable URL.

The health app's privacy policy, together with in-app disclosures, must comprehensively disclose access, collection, use and sharing of personal and sensitive data beyond what the Data safety section lists.
Health apps must meet the prominent disclosure and consent requirements for any functionality or data covered by dangerous or runtime permissions.
Health apps should not request permissions that their core functionality does not need, and must remove unused permissions.

Apps that are not primarily health apps but access health data (such as insurers or games using activity data) should make the link between their core functionality and the health data clear to users, and their privacy policy must reflect that limited use.
Apps must not offer health or medical functionality that is misleading or potentially harmful.
Apps that need external hardware (such as a blood glucose monitor) for their medical function must disclose that requirement in the description and must not imply they work without it.
Apps that use device sensors such as the camera for health functions must state in the description which devices are compatible, for example which models support sensor-only oximetry.

Apps regulated as medical devices must declare themselves as such in Play Console with the required information and provide proof of approval, clearance or certification from the relevant authority on request.

Health and medical apps that are not regulated medical devices must state in the app description that the app is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any medical condition, and must remind users to consult a healthcare professional for medical advice, diagnosis or treatment.
Apps developed in affiliation with a government or recognized healthcare organization must submit proof of eligibility through the advance notice form.
Contact tracing and health status apps must select Disease Prevention and Public Health in Play Console and submit the advance notice form.

Apps doing health-related human subjects research must follow all applicable rules and obtain informed consent from participants (or a parent or guardian for minors), and should also have IRB or equivalent ethics approval unless exempt, with proof provided on request.
Data accessed through Health Connect permissions is personal and sensitive data subject to the User Data policy and the additional Health Connect requirements.
Apps must not facilitate the sale or purchase of prescription drugs without a prescription.

Apps must not promote or sell unapproved substances regardless of claimed legality, including listed prohibited pharmaceuticals and supplements, ephedra products, hCG for weight loss or with anabolic steroids, supplements with active pharmaceutical or dangerous ingredients, products subject to regulatory action or warnings, and products with names confusingly similar to unapproved or controlled substances.
Apps must not make false or misleading health claims, such as implying a product is as effective as prescription drugs or that an unapproved product prevents, cures or treats a disease.

Apps must not contain misleading health claims that contradict medical consensus or can cause harm, such as false vaccine claims, advocacy of harmful unapproved treatments or harmful practices like conversion therapy.
Transactions for regulated clinical services should not use Google Play's billing system.

title: Intellectual Property
requirements: All content in the app and its store listing must be the developer's original work or used under a license or permission the developer can document.

Apps must not infringe copyright, and modifying copyrighted material may still be a violation; for example album, game or book cover art, film or TV marketing images, comic or cartoon artwork, sports team logos, photos of public figures taken from their social media or professional shoots, fan art indistinguishable from the original, soundboards of copyrighted audio clips, and full reproductions or translations of books not in the public domain.

Apps must not induce or encourage copyright infringement, such as streaming apps that let users save local copies of copyrighted content without authorization, and the description and screenshots must not promote unauthorized downloading or streaming.
Apps and listings must not use another party's trademark (name, logo, brand) in a way likely to confuse users about the source of the product.
Apps must not sell or promote for sale counterfeit goods bearing a trademark or logo identical or substantially indistinguishable from another brand's.
Apps and developer accounts must not infringe patents, trade secrets or other proprietary rights of others.

Developers who use third-party intellectual property with written permission (brand names, logos, graphic assets) should contact the Google Play team with that documentation before submitting, to avoid rejection.

title: User Data
requirements: Apps must disclose how they access, collect, use, handle and share user data (including device information) and limit use to the disclosed, policy-compliant purposes.
Apps must comply with the privacy and data protection laws of every jurisdiction where they are offered.

Developers must ensure that bundled third-party code such as SDKs, and third-party AI integrations, handle user data from the app in line with Play policy, including use, disclosure, consent and limited-use rules, and that SDK providers do not sell personal and sensitive data.

Apps and their SDKs must not link persistent device identifiers (such as IMEI, IMSI or SIM serial) to personal and sensitive data or to resettable identifiers, except for SIM-linked telephony or enterprise device management in device owner mode, and those exceptions must be prominently disclosed.

Apps must limit access, collection, use and sharing of personal and sensitive data (such as identifiers, financial and authentication data, contacts, location, SMS and call data, health data, installed app inventory, microphone, camera and screen content) to app functionality and purposes users would reasonably expect, transferring it only to service providers, for legal reasons or in a merger with adequate notice; ads use must follow the Ads policy.
Apps must handle personal and sensitive data securely, including transmitting it with modern cryptography such as HTTPS.
Apps must use a runtime permission request, where one exists, before accessing data gated by an Android permission.
Apps must not sell personal and sensitive user data, meaning transfer to a third party for money; user-initiated transfers are not a sale.

When data access, collection, use or sharing may fall outside users' reasonable expectations (for example background collection), apps must show an in-app disclosure during normal use, not only in the listing, a website, a menu, a privacy policy or terms, that describes the data and how it is used and shared and is not bundled with unrelated disclosures.

The consent request or runtime permission prompt must immediately follow that disclosure, must be clear, must require an affirmative action such as a tap or checkbox, must not treat navigating away, back, home or an auto-dismissing or expiring message as consent, and must be granted before any collection or access starts.
Apps relying on a legal basis other than consent (such as GDPR legitimate interest) must still meet applicable legal requirements and provide the required in-app disclosures.

Apps integrating an SDK that collects personal and sensitive data by default must be able to show Google, within two weeks of a request, that the prominent disclosure and consent requirements are met for that SDK's data handling.
Apps must never publicly disclose financial or payment data or government identification numbers, and must not publish or disclose people's non-public contacts without authorization.

Apps with anti-virus, anti-malware or other security features must post a privacy policy that, with any in-app disclosures, explains what data is collected and transmitted, how it is used and the types of parties it is shared with.
Apps that target children must not include SDKs that are not approved for child-directed services.
Every app must have a clear, accurate and up-to-date Data safety section in Play Console covering collection, use and sharing (including by SDKs), consistent with the privacy policy.
Every app, including apps that access no personal and sensitive data, must provide a privacy policy link in the designated Play Console field and a privacy policy link or text inside the app.

The privacy policy, together with in-app disclosures, must fully describe data access, collection, use and sharing beyond what the Data safety section lists, including developer information and a privacy contact or inquiry mechanism, the types of personal and sensitive data and the parties it is shared with, secure handling procedures, and the retention and deletion policy.
The privacy policy must be clearly labeled as a privacy policy and must name the entity shown in the store listing or the app itself.
The privacy policy must be hosted at an active, publicly accessible, non-geofenced URL, must not be a PDF and must not be editable.

Apps that let users create an account from within the app must let users request account deletion through a readily discoverable option both inside the app and outside it (for example a website), with the web resource link entered in the Play Console field.
Deleting an account at the user's request must also delete the associated user data, and temporary deactivation, disabling or freezing does not count as deletion.
Apps that retain some data after deletion for legitimate reasons such as security, fraud prevention or regulatory compliance must clearly disclose that retention, for example in the privacy policy.

The account deletion process must not contain hidden steps or undue obstacles, the external deletion link must not be broken or outdated, and the deletion resource must clearly reference the app or service.

Apps must not use the App Set ID for ads personalization or ads measurement, must not connect it to Android identifiers such as the AAID or to personal and sensitive data for advertising, and must disclose its collection and use in a legally adequate privacy notice including the privacy policy, obtaining consent where legally required.

Apps that process personal information made available by Google originating in the EEA, UK or Switzerland must comply with applicable data protection law, process it only consistently with the individual's consent, protect it with appropriate technical and organizational measures, provide the protection level required by the Data Privacy Framework Principles, monitor compliance, and notify Google and stop or remediate processing if they cannot meet these conditions.

title: Deceptive Behavior
requirements: Apps must not be functionally impossible or claim impossible features (for example insect repellent or phone breathalyzer apps), and labelling the app a prank, joke or for entertainment does not exempt it.

The description, title, icon, screenshots and video must accurately and clearly describe the app's actual functionality; for example a puzzle game must not be presented as a racing game, and a text guide must not be presented as an antivirus app.
The app's category and content rating must be set correctly.
Apps must not contain demonstrably false or deceptive content that may interfere with voting processes or about election outcomes.

Apps must not falsely claim affiliation with a government entity or to provide government services they are not authorized to provide, nor claim to be the official app of an established entity without the rights to do so.
Apps and their ads must not mimic functionality or warnings of the operating system or other apps, including ads styled as system notifications or warnings.
Apps must not mimic other apps or websites to trick users into disclosing personal or authentication information.

Apps must not change device settings or features outside the app (system or browser settings, bookmarks, shortcuts, icons, widgets, homescreen presentation) without the user's knowledge and explicit consent, and must explain what will change and why.
Any consented change to device settings or features must be easily reversible by the user.
Apps and ads must not modify device settings or features as a service to third parties or for advertising purposes.

Apps must not mislead users into removing or disabling third-party apps or changing device settings, and must not encourage or incentivize such removal or changes unless it is part of a verifiable security service.
Apps must not help users deceive others, including generating or facilitating ID cards, social security numbers, passports, diplomas, credit cards, bank accounts or driver's licenses.
Apps should perform as users would reasonably expect from their disclosures, title, description and images.

Apps may download additional resources (such as game assets) only when needed for use of the app, those resources must comply with all Play policies, and the app must prompt the user and disclose the download size before starting the download, including CDN downloads.
Apps must not display unverified or real phone numbers, contacts, addresses or other personally identifiable information of non-consenting people or entities.
Apps whose core functionality differs by geography, device parameters or other user-dependent data must prominently disclose those differences in the store listing.
Apps that change significantly between versions must alert users (for example in What's new) and update the store listing.

Apps must not create, promote or help create demonstrably misleading imagery, audio, video or text that may cause harm regarding sensitive events, politics, social issues or public concern; exceptions exist for public interest, clearly artificial images, obvious satire or parody, and media carrying user-facing disclaimers or watermarks.
Apps that manipulate media must still comply with all other Play policies, including Restricted Content, and must not have creating misleading media as their sole purpose.
Apps must not alter media to mimic a news broadcast using real outlet names or logos, or add public figures to clips, without a clear watermark or disclaimer.
Store listings must not use public figures or media from sensitive events to advertise media-altering capabilities.
Apps must not contain hidden, dormant or undocumented features (including ones activated remotely or after a delay), and all user-facing features should be clear and documented in the listing.

Apps must behave the same for reviewers as for users: no detection of the review environment, no modifying or obfuscating behavior during review, no code obfuscation to conceal violations, and no misleading reviewers about purpose or functionality.
Apps must not dynamically download and execute remote code that introduces features or functionality not present during review.
All code in the app, including third-party SDKs, should relate to the app's stated purpose, and the developer must be able to provide Google with details of features and code on request.

title: Impersonation
requirements: The developer name, app title, icon, description and in-app elements must not falsely imply a relationship with, or authorization by, another developer, company, organization or app; for example a developer name suggesting an official tie to Google.
Icons and titles must not use national emblems or copy a business's logo to suggest government affiliation or an official app of that business.
App titles and icons must not be so similar to existing products, services, websites or TV shows that users could be misled about affiliation.
Apps must not claim to be the official app of an established entity or person (for example "X Official") without the necessary rights or permission.
Apps must comply with the Android Brand Guidelines.
Developers must not conceal their identity or the app's primary purpose, and must not coordinate with others to mislead users, especially on political or social content.

title: Device and Network Abuse
requirements: Apps and their SDKs must not interfere with, disrupt, damage or gain unauthorized access to the user's device, other devices, servers, networks, APIs or services, including other apps, Google services and carrier networks.
Apps must meet the default Android system optimization requirements in the Core App Quality guidelines.
Apps distributed on Google Play must not modify, replace or update themselves by any means other than Google Play's update mechanism.

Apps and their SDKs must not download executable code such as dex, JAR or .so files from any source other than Google Play; code run in a VM or interpreter with only indirect Android API access (such as JavaScript in a WebView) is excepted, but runtime-loaded interpreted code must not enable policy violations.
Apps must not contain code that introduces or exploits security vulnerabilities.
Apps and their SDKs must not load untrusted content (such as http:// URLs) or unverified URLs from untrusted sources (such as untrusted Intents) in a WebView that has an added JavaScript interface.

Apps must not block or interfere with ads shown by other apps, provide game cheats that affect other apps, or facilitate or instruct hacking of services, software or hardware or circumvention of security protections.
Apps must not access or use a service or API in a way that violates its terms of service.
Apps that are not eligible for allowlisting must not try to bypass system power management.
Apps may provide proxy services to third parties only when proxying is the app's primary user-facing core purpose.
Apps must not install other apps without the user's prior consent, and must not link to or facilitate the distribution or installation of malicious software.
Apps must not use the full-screen intent permission to force interaction with disruptive ads or notifications.
Apps must not circumvent Android sandbox protections to infer user activity or identity from other apps.

Apps targeting Android 14+ must declare a valid foreground service type and its matching permission for each foreground service, and complete the Play Console declaration describing each use, including its user impact and a demo video.

Apps may declare a foreground service permission only when the use is a user-beneficial core feature, is user-initiated or perceptible, can be stopped by the user, cannot be deferred or interrupted by the system without harming the experience, and runs only as long as needed; systemExempted, shortService and dataSync used for Play Asset Delivery are exempt.
Apps may use the user-initiated data transfer jobs API only for user-initiated network data transfers that run only as long as the transfer requires.

Apps must respect other apps' FLAG_SECURE and must not facilitate or build workarounds to bypass it; accessibility tools are exempt only if they never transmit, save or cache protected content for access outside the device.

Apps that provide on-device Android containers must check loaded apps for the REQUIRE_SECURE_ENV manifest flag, must not load apps that declare it, must not proxy device APIs to make apps appear installed in the container, and must not bypass the flag (for example by loading an older version).

title: Malware
requirements: Apps, including all bundled third-party code such as SDKs, must not contain any code that puts users, their data or their devices at risk, such as trojans, phishing or spyware, even unintentionally.

Apps must not contain backdoor code that enables unwanted, potentially harmful remote-controlled operations, including dynamic code loading or arbitrary code execution used to perform behavior of any other malware category.

Apps must not charge users deceptively: no premium SMS or premium calls without consent, no hiding or obscuring billing disclosures or suppressing carrier charge or subscription messages, and no toll fraud through carrier billing, WAP (for example taps on hidden WebViews) or airtime transfer.

Apps that collect and transmit personal data to a third party for monitoring are allowed only if exclusively designed and marketed for parents monitoring children or enterprises monitoring employees, and must never be usable to track other people such as a spouse, even with consent.

Monitoring apps must declare the isMonitoringTool manifest flag, must not present themselves as spying or secret surveillance tools or hide tracking behavior, must show a persistent notification while running and a unique identifying icon, must disclose monitoring in the Play description, and must provide prominent disclosure and consent.
Monitoring apps and their listings must not offer any way to unlock non-compliant functionality, such as links to non-compliant APKs hosted outside Google Play, and must comply with applicable laws.
Apps must not, without the user's knowledge, take part in denial-of-service attacks or generate excessive traffic against other systems.

Apps must not be hostile downloaders, meaning code believed to be built to spread PHAs that has downloaded them or can download and install apps, or code where at least 5% of at least 500 observed downloads are PHAs; major browsers and file-sharing apps are exempt only if they do not drive downloads without user interaction and every PHA download is started by a consenting user.
Apps must not impersonate a trustworthy source to request credentials or billing information and send it to a third party, or intercept credentials in transit.

Apps must not break the app sandbox or gain elevated privileges, including violating the Android permissions model, stealing credentials such as OAuth tokens from other apps, preventing their own uninstallation or stopping, or disabling SELinux.
Apps must not lock users out of their device, encrypt their data, or abuse device admin features to block removal in order to demand payment or action.
Apps that root the device must tell the user in advance and must not perform any other harmful behavior; rooting without notice is prohibited.
Apps must not send unsolicited messages to the user's contacts or use the device as an email spam relay.

Apps and their SDKs must not collect, exfiltrate or share user or device data unrelated to policy-compliant functionality, or without adequate notice and consent, including recording audio or calls or stealing app data.
Apps must not hide harmful functionality behind an innocuous purpose, and must not use obfuscation, dynamic code loading or cloaking to behave differently for reviewers than for regular users.
Apps must not contain components that are threats to non-Android platforms.

title: Misrepresentation
requirements: Apps and developer accounts must not impersonate any person or organization.
Apps and developer accounts must not misrepresent or conceal their ownership or primary purpose; the title, icon and description must honestly represent functionality and purpose.

The developer name, organization, contact information and country of origin in the account must be accurate; developers must not misrepresent or conceal their country of origin while directing content at users in another country.

Apps and accounts must not coordinate with other apps, sites, developers or accounts to conceal or misrepresent developer or app identity or other material details where the content relates to politics, social issues or matters of public concern.

title: Google Play Families Policies
requirements: Before publishing, developers must declare the app's target audience in the Play Console Target audience and content section and should select only age groups the app is designed for and appropriate for (for example only Ages 5 and under for apps for babies, toddlers and preschoolers, and mixed adult and child groups only if truly designed for all ages); child-oriented imagery and terminology may affect Google's assessment of the declared audience.

Apps that include children in their target audience must answer Play Console questions accurately, including Target audience and content, Data safety and the IARC content rating questionnaire, and keep those answers updated as the app changes.

Content in apps that include children in their target audience must be appropriate for children wherever children can access it, for example no adult-only content behind a child-friendly listing, no glamorized alcohol, tobacco or controlled substances, no real or simulated gambling, no inappropriate violence or gore, no dating or sexual or marital advice, and no links to sites with policy-violating content.
Apps that include children in their target audience must not merely wrap a website in a WebView or primarily drive affiliate traffic to a website without the site owner's permission.

Apps that include children in their target audience must disclose any collection of personal and sensitive information from children, including through APIs and SDKs, such as authentication data, microphone and camera data, device data, Android ID and ad usage data.
Apps that solely target children must not transmit AAID, SIM serial, build serial, BSSID, MAC, SSID, IMEI or IMSI, and should not request the AD_ID permission when targeting API 33 or higher.
Apps that target both children and older users must not transmit AAID, SIM serial, build serial, BSSID, MAC, SSID, IMEI or IMSI from children or users of unknown age.
Apps that include children in their target audience must not request the device phone number from TelephonyManager.
Apps that solely target children must not request location permission or collect, use or transmit precise location.
Apps that include children in their target audience must use the Companion Device Manager when requesting Bluetooth, unless they only target OS versions that do not support it.
Apps that solely target children must not contain APIs or SDKs not approved for child-directed services.

Apps that target both children and older users may use APIs or SDKs not approved for child-directed services only behind a neutral age screen or in a way that collects no data from children, and must not require users to access content through such an API or SDK.

Apps that include children in their target audience and use augmented reality must show a safety warning as soon as the AR section launches, which should cover parental supervision and awareness of real-world physical hazards, and must not require devices advised against for children.
Apps that include children in their target audience and let users share or exchange information must disclose those features accurately in the content rating questionnaire.

Social apps and apps with social features that include children in their target audience must show an in-app reminder about online safety and real-world risks before children can exchange freeform media or information, and must require adult action (an adult verification mechanism that does not encourage age falsification) before children can exchange personal information.
Apps with social features that include children in their target audience must give adults a way to manage those features for child users, such as enabling, disabling or limiting them.
Apps whose main focus is chatting with strangers or anonymously, such as chat roulette, dating, open kids chat rooms or anonymous messaging apps, must not target children.
Apps that include children in their target audience, including the APIs and SDKs they use, must comply with COPPA, GDPR and other applicable laws.

Apps that show ads to children or users of unknown age must use only Families self-certified ads SDKs for those users (in mixed-audience apps behind an age screening measure such as a neutral age screen), with no interest-based advertising or remarketing and only child-appropriate ad content (no mature media or games, harmful substances, gambling or sweepstakes, sexual content, dating or graphic violence).

In apps that solely target children, and for children or unknown-age users in mixed-audience apps, monetization must not be disruptive or undismissable (such as ad walls), must be closeable after 5 seconds if it interrupts normal use (including rewarded ads), must not show interstitials at app launch, must not show multiple ad placements on a page, must be clearly distinguishable from content (no offerwalls or immersive ads, no promotions that look like app content), must not use shocking or manipulative tactics for ad views or purchases, and must not trick users into clicks through dismiss buttons or ads that appear where users tap.

Apps that include children in their target audience must clearly distinguish virtual game currency from real money for in-app purchases, must avoid overly aggressive commercial tactics, and must keep all ads, cross-promotions, in-app purchase offers and paid placements compliant with applicable laws and industry guidelines.

title: User Ratings, Reviews, and Installs
requirements: Apps must not offer rewards or incentives (such as a discount) in exchange for ratings or reviews.
Rating prompts must be clear and non-deceptive, and apps must not use deceptive pop-ups or force users to rate the app.
Developers must not inflate ratings, reviews or install counts by illegitimate means, including posing as users to submit repeated ratings or using automated services.
Apps must not have incentivizing users to install other apps as their main functionality.
