Developers must not submit, or encourage users to submit, reviews containing inappropriate content such as affiliate offers, coupons, game codes, email addresses, or links to websites or other apps.
As a best practice, developer replies to reviews should stay focused on the issues the user raised and should not ask for a higher rating.

title: Functionality, Content, and User Experience
requirements: Apps must provide app-specific functionality and adequate content; static text-only or PDF-only apps, apps with very little content such as a single wallpaper, and apps designed to do nothing are not allowed.
Apps must install, load and respond to the user without crashing, force closing, freezing or otherwise functioning abnormally.
Apps should provide a stable, responsive and engaging experience with unique and meaningful functionality.

title: Metadata
requirements: The description, developer name, title, icon, screenshots and promotional images must not be misleading, improperly formatted, non-descriptive, irrelevant, excessive or inappropriate, and screenshots and videos should reflect the actual app experience.

The app must have a clear, well-written description that accurately describes its functionality; keeping it succinct is a best practice, though excessive length, detail, improper formatting or repetition can still violate the policy.
The description must not contain unattributed or anonymous user testimonials.
The description must not contain repetitive or unrelated keywords or references, word blocks, vertical or horizontal word lists, or data comparisons with other apps or brands.
The title, icon and developer name must not contain emojis, emoticons (including kaomojis), repeated or irrelevant special characters, or ALL CAPS unless part of the brand name.
The app title must be 30 characters or fewer.

The title, icon and developer name must not contain text or images indicating store performance or ranking (such as #1, App of the year, Best of Play, Popular, award icons), price or promotions (such as 10% off, cash back, free for a limited time), or Google Play programs (such as Editor's choice, New).
App icons must not use misleading symbols, such as a new-message dot when there are no new messages or a download or install symbol when the app is not about downloading content.

Listing text, images and videos must be suitable for a general audience, with no sexually suggestive imagery, profane or vulgar language, prominently depicted graphic violence, or illicit drug use, and this applies even to Educational, Documentary, Scientific or Artistic content.
Listings must not make deceptive superlative claims (such as "best game ever") or use a celebrity's name or a brand's logo without permission.
Apps must provide any additional metadata that specific Developer Program Policies require.

title: Content Ratings
requirements: Every app on Google Play must have an IARC content rating, obtained by completing the Play Console rating questionnaire for each new app and each existing active app; unrated apps are removed.
Answers to the content rating questionnaire must accurately represent the app's content.
A new questionnaire must be submitted whenever changes to app content or features affect the previous answers.
Ads shown in the app must not be significantly more mature than the app's primary content.
Developers must inform users of age-based considerations not covered by the content rating, such as age-specific privacy practices.

title: App Promotion
requirements: Apps must not engage in or benefit from promotion practices, such as ads, that are deceptive or harmful or that violate Developer Program Policies, wherever the promotion runs (websites, apps or other properties).
Promotion must not use ads resembling system notifications or alerts, or misleading text or imagery to elicit downloads.
Apps must not be promoted with sexually explicit ads directing users to the Play listing.
Promotion or installation tactics must not redirect users to Google Play or download apps without informed user action.
Apps must not be promoted through unsolicited SMS.
The title, icon and developer name must not contain text or images indicating store performance or ranking, price or promotions, or ties to Google Play programs.
Developers are responsible for ensuring that ad networks, affiliates and ads associated with the app comply with these rules.

title: Spam
requirements: Apps must not send SMS, email or other messages on the user's behalf (for example from a Share button) without letting the user confirm the content and recipients.
Apps must not have as their primary purpose driving affiliate or referral traffic to a website to earn credit for sign-ups or purchases.
Apps must not have as their primary purpose providing a webview of a website without permission from its owner or administrator.
Apps must not merely copy content or the experience of other apps without adding original value, and should provide value through unique content or services.
Developers must not publish multiple apps with highly similar functionality, content and user experience; small apps of this kind should be combined into a single app.

title: Enforcement Process
requirements: Developers are responsible for ensuring that third-party code in the app, such as SDKs, and the third party's practices with respect to the app comply with all Developer Program Policies.

A rejected or removed app must not be resubmitted or republished until all its policy violations are fixed, and because notices may not list every violation, developers must check the rest of the app, account and catalog for compliance.
Developers whose account is terminated must not register a new Play Console account.
Developer accounts must stay actively used (publishing or updating apps, viewing statistics, managing listings) to avoid closure as dormant accounts, which are not in good standing.

title: Policy Coverage
requirements: Play policies apply to all content the app displays or links to, including ads it shows and user-generated content it hosts or links to.
The developer name and the landing page of the developer website listed on Google Play must comply with Play policies.
Apps must not let users install other apps onto their devices.
Apps that give access to other apps, games or software without installation, including third-party features and experiences, must ensure all that content complies with Play policies.
App content must be rated in accordance with the Content Rating Guidelines.
Apps and app content must not undermine user trust in the Google Play ecosystem.

title: Android Instant Apps
requirements: Instant apps with login functionality must integrate Smart Lock for Passwords.
When an instant app or installed app contains links that can resolve to an instant app, it must send users to that instant app rather than capturing the links, for example in a WebView.
Instant apps must comply with the Android Instant Apps technical specifications and requirements in Google's documentation.

An instant app may offer the installable app but this must not be its primary purpose, and the install button must use the Material Design get app icon with the label install, with no more than 2 to 3 implicit install prompts and no banner or ad-like install prompts.
Instant apps must not make device changes that persist beyond the instant app session, such as changing the wallpaper or adding a homescreen widget.
Instant apps must remain visible so the user knows at all times that the instant app is running.

Instant apps must not access device identifiers that both persist after the app stops and cannot be reset by the user (such as Build Serial, network MAC addresses, IMEI or IMSI), may access the phone number only through the runtime permission, and must not fingerprint the user by any means.
All network traffic from an instant app must be encrypted with TLS, such as HTTPS.

title: Subscriptions
requirements: Apps must not mislead users about subscriptions or use deceptive or manipulative purchase experiences, and must communicate clearly in in-app promotions, splash screens and plan selection screens, with all stated subscription benefits truthful and accurate.

Subscription offers must clearly and explicitly disclose the offer terms, the cost, the billing frequency, the automatic renewal terms (for example that a monthly plan renews and charges every month), whether a subscription is needed to use the app, and other material information, and users should not have to take any extra action to review it.

Subscription offers must prominently show the amount the user will actually be charged, not mainly a monthly breakdown of an annual or multi-month price, and must not show only an introductory price without the later recurring price.
Subscription pricing and terms must be fully localized to the user's language and currency.
Subscription offers must have a clearly visible dismiss option and, when content is available without subscribing, must clearly show that users can access it without a subscription or trial.

Subscriptions must deliver sustained or recurring value for their whole life, with any bonuses complementary to that value, and products offering one-time benefits (such as lump-sum credits or single-use boosters) must be sold as in-app products rather than subscriptions.

Developers must not disguise one-time benefits as subscriptions, including by cancelling, deprecating or minimizing a subscription's recurring value after purchase, or by selling an auto-renewing subscription for a one-time benefit and then cancelling it without the user's request.
Subscription SKU names must accurately describe the product and must not use labels like Free Trial for subscriptions that carry an auto-recurring charge.
Purchase flows must not lead users into accidentally subscribing, for example through repeated taps in the same button area across multiple screens or charges that are hard to read.

Before enrolling a user in a free trial or introductory offer, apps must clearly state its duration, price and included content, when and how it converts to a paid subscription, the paid price, and how to cancel before conversion.

Apps selling subscriptions must clearly explain how users can manage or cancel them and must give in-app access to an easy online cancellation method, for example a link to the Google Play Subscription Center or direct access to the cancellation process in account settings.
Developers must notify users of changes to their subscription, cancellation and refund policies and keep those policies compliant with applicable law.

announced.text: Subscriptions with ongoing eligibility-based discounts, such as student plans, must clearly disclose the eligibility criteria, the verification process, and how pricing and benefits change once the user is no longer eligible.

title: Families Self-Certified Ads SDK Program
requirements: Apps whose target audience includes only children and that use ads SDKs to serve ads must use only ads SDK versions that are self-certified under the Families Self-Certified Ads SDK program.
Apps whose target audience includes both children and older users must ensure, for example with a neutral age screen, that ads shown to children come only from self-certified ads SDK versions.
Developers remain responsible for ensuring every SDK version they use, including self-certified ones, complies with policies and applicable laws.

In-house cross-promotion of the developer's own apps or media and direct deals with advertisers managed through SDKs do not require a self-certified ads SDK, but the ad content and data collection must still comply with the User Data and Families policies.

Ads SDKs seeking self-certification must register in Play SDK Console committing not to cause policy violations, define and prohibit objectionable ad content, rate creatives into age groups including at least Everyone and Mature, and offer per-request or per-app child-directed treatment that disables personalized, interest-based and remarketing ads in line with COPPA and GDPR.

Self-certified ads SDKs must let publishers select Families-compliant ad formats, review creatives and propagate privacy indicators when real-time bidding serves children, give Google a test app and requested information, certify every new release, and publish technical documentation for compliant implementation.
Mediation platforms serving ads to children must use only self-certified ads SDKs or equivalent safeguards and must pass the ad content rating and child-directed treatment to mediated networks.

title: News & Magazines
requirements: Apps that declare themselves News or Magazine in Play Console, or that list in the News and Magazine category and call themselves news or magazine in the title, icon, developer name or description, must declare as News & Magazine and complete the Play Console self-declaration.
News & Magazine apps must identify the source of each article, including its original publisher or author.
News & Magazine apps must update their content regularly and not offer static content.
News & Magazine apps must give users clear, easy access to up-to-date contact information for the app.
News & Magazine apps that show third-party content (for example aggregators) must clearly tell users the publishing sources of that content.
News & Magazine apps that require a membership or subscription must offer an in-app content preview before purchase.
News & Magazine apps must not have affiliate marketing or ad revenue as their primary purpose.

title: Unauthorized Use or Imitation of System Functionality
requirements: Apps and their ads must not mimic or interfere with system functionality such as system notifications or warnings, and must not create notifications or alerts that look like they come from the operating system.

Apps may use system-level notifications only for the app's own integral features (such as an airline's deals or a game's in-game promotions), clearly attributed to the app, and must not use them to serve ads or promote a different app or third-party service.

title: Ad Fraud
requirements: Apps must not generate ad interactions designed to make ad networks believe traffic comes from genuine user interest, whether through bots, scripts, altered information or human activity designed to produce invalid traffic.
Apps must not render ads that are hidden, off-screen or otherwise invisible to the user.
Apps must not automatically generate ad clicks without user intent, or network traffic equivalent to clicks, and must not implement ads in ways that trick users into accidental clicks.
Apps must not send fake install attribution clicks to claim credit for installs that did not come from their network.
Apps must not pop up ads when the user is not inside the app's interface.
Apps must represent their ad inventory accurately to ad networks, including the real platform (for example not claiming iOS when running on Android) and the actual package name being monetized.

title: Mobile Unwanted Software
requirements: Apps should deliver every function they promise, be clear about their purpose and functionality, and tell users about all of their principal and significant functions.
Apps must not trick users into installing them or piggyback on the installation of other software, and must disclose any software bundled with them.
Apps must clearly explain any system changes they make and let users review and approve all significant installation options and changes.
Apps must not misrepresent the state of the device, for example by claiming it is in a critical security state or infected with viruses.
Apps must not generate invalid activity intended to inflate ad traffic or conversions.
Apps must not impersonate another developer, company, entity or app, or imply a relationship with or authorization from someone they are not related to.
Apps must be transparent about accessing, collecting, using and sharing personal and sensitive data, handle it securely (for example transmitting over HTTPS), and follow the User Data policies.
Apps must not ask or trick users into turning off device protections such as Google Play Protect, including by offering features or rewards in exchange.
Apps must not show ads in unexpected ways that impair device functions, or display ads outside the triggering app's environment without easy dismissal, adequate consent and attribution.
Apps must not interfere with other apps or the usability of the device, and uninstalling them must be clear where applicable.
Apps must not mimic prompts from the operating system or other apps, and must not suppress alerts from other apps or the OS, especially alerts about OS changes.

title: Google Play Policies | Android Developers
requirements: Developers of anonymous chat apps must not target children under the Families policy requirements.
Anonymous chat and random chat apps are subject to the Age-Restricted Content and Functionality policy.
Anonymous chat and random chat apps are subject to the Child Safety Standards policy.

Under Android developer verification (effective September 30, 2026), apps from participating stores in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand must be registered by a verified developer to install on certified Android devices, and Play developers should check the Play Console Home page to register any remaining apps to avoid global removal from Google Play.

announced.text: Geofencing is no longer an approved foreground service use case; developers can use the Geofence API instead.
Under the new Contacts Permission policy, apps that do not need broad access to the user's contacts must use the Android Contact Picker.

Apps targeting API 37+ must use the Android location button for one-time or infrequent precise location requests, and apps whose core functionality needs broader ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION must file a Play Console declaration justifying why the button or coarse location is insufficient.

Account verification by phone call is no longer a permitted use of READ_CALL_LOG; apps must use the Digital Credentials API (directly or via a provider built on it), the SMS Retriever API, or another listed alternative.
Subscriptions with ongoing eligibility-based discounts, such as student plans, must clearly disclose eligibility criteria, the verification process, and post-eligibility price and benefit changes.
Apps building AppFunctions must comply with all Play policies, and AppFunctions must not deceive or manipulate AI agents, bypass security controls, or interfere with other apps.
The Local Network permission is limited to apps whose core functionality needs it where device pickers are insufficient, and apps targeting API 37+ must file a Play Console declaration to use it.

The Manage Contacts permission is limited to apps whose core functionality needs it where system pickers are insufficient and requires a Play Console declaration; other apps must use narrowly scoped platform intents.

title: Google Play
requirements: The developer must accept the Distribution Agreement and keep complete, current and accurate information in Play Console, and all information given to Google or users about the developer or its products must be true, accurate, supportable and complete (2.1, 11.4).
The developer must be verified and in good standing before products can be distributed, and a person accepting on behalf of an organization must have authority to bind it (2.2, 2.3).
The developer and its products must comply with the Developer Program Policies (4.1).
To charge for products, the developer must hold a valid Payments Profile approved by a Payment Processor and keep it in good standing (3.2).

The developer is responsible for accurate tax inputs and tax categorization of products in Play Console, must supply requested tax documents such as IRS Form W-9 or W-8, and, unless resident in the United States or Singapore, must give Google 90 days' written notice before services in a product are performed there (3.5, 3.6).
Products first offered free must stay free, and any extra charge must relate to an alternative or supplemental version of the product (3.7).
Users must be able to reinstall each product without any additional fee, except products removed for a Legal Takedown, which users can no longer reinstall (3.9).
The developer must provide required product information, support users, and accurately disclose the permissions the product needs to function on devices (4.2).
The developer must keep its developer credentials confidential and is responsible for all products built under them (4.3).
Products must not have a purpose that facilitates distributing Android apps or games outside Google Play (4.5).

The developer must use Google Play only for lawful purposes and comply with all applicable laws worldwide, including export control and sanctions regulations on destinations, users and end use (4.6, 11.3, 16.5).

Each product's detail page must show valid, accurate developer contact information for customer support and legal purposes, and the developer must handle support, maintenance and complaints for its products (4.7).
For paid products or in-app transactions, the developer must answer support inquiries within 3 business days and within 24 hours for issues Google flags as urgent (4.7).

Products that receive or access login credentials or personal information must tell users that this information is available to the product, provide a legally adequate privacy notice and protection, use the data only for the purposes the user permitted, and store personal or sensitive data securely and only as long as needed, unless a separate user agreement covering data directly related to the product governs (4.8).
Products given Google Account information may use it only to access the user's Google Account when and for the limited purposes the user permitted (4.8).
Products must not interfere with, disrupt, damage or access without authorization any devices, servers, networks or services of third parties, including Google (4.9).
Any end user license agreement included in a product is subordinate to the Distribution Agreement where they conflict (5.3).

The developer must hold the intellectual property rights in its products, including the right to monetize them on its own behalf, and must not submit third-party material without owning the rights or having the owner's permission (11.1, 11.2).
Android Brand Features may be used only for marketing and only in line with the Android Brand Guidelines (6.4).

After removing a product, the developer must still honor the Agreement and Payments Profile terms for prior sales, including refunds, and keep delivering and supporting products and services users already bought (8.1).
If a product is removed for a Legal Takedown, the developer must, at Google's request, refund users who bought it within the previous year or a longer period required by local consumer law (8.2).

Rights under the Agreement may not be assigned or transferred without the other party's prior approval, except through a change of control, which may lead Google to terminate the Agreement (16.6, 16.7).
A developer that terminates the Agreement must unpublish all its products and stop using Play Console and its developer credentials (10.2).

title: Understanding Google Play’s app account deletion requirements
requirements: All developers must complete the Data deletion questions in the Play Console Data safety form, and apps within scope must state whether they offer account deletion and provide the deletion web link there.

Apps that let users create an app account, either directly in the app or by sending them to an external account creation flow, must offer account deletion even if parts of the app work without an account; permanently private apps, enterprise device management apps and accounts created and operated purely offline are out of scope.

Apps in scope must provide an in-app path for users to delete their account and associated data, which should be prominent and intuitive (for example in account settings) and may be a link to the web deletion resource rather than a fully in-app flow.

Apps in scope must provide a web resource where users can request account and data deletion, for example through a deletion link, a support email or a request form, and it should not require users to return to or reinstall the app.

The deletion web link must load without errors, feature the deletion pathway prominently, and reference the app or developer name exactly as shown on the store listing; if an existing privacy or retention page is reused, its deletion section should be highlighted and reasonably prominent, for example with an anchor link.
Any steps required before deletion, such as cancelling a subscription, must be clearly explained, with a support flow users can start.

When an account is deleted at the user's request, the associated user data, including all data declared as collected in the Data safety section, must be deleted except data retained for legitimate reasons such as security, fraud prevention or regulatory compliance, and service providers that process the data should be asked to delete it too.
Apps that offer account creation should tell users what to expect from a deletion request and fulfil it within a reasonably quick period, while checking any local legal deletion or retention rules.

Apps that retain some data for security, fraud prevention or regulatory compliance, or that face longer regulated retention periods, must clearly disclose those retention practices, for example in the privacy policy.
Non-mobile surfaces such as Android TV or Wear OS may omit the in-app deletion option but must still offer a discoverable web deletion resource entered in the Play Console URL field.

title: Understanding foreground service and full-screen intent requirements
requirements: Apps targeting Android 14+ must declare a foreground service type in the manifest for every foreground service they use, together with the matching FOREGROUND_SERVICE_* permission (for example FOREGROUND_SERVICE_CAMERA for the camera type).

Apps targeting Android 14+ must also meet any runtime prerequisites of the chosen foreground service type, such as holding a coarse or fine location grant before starting a location foreground service.

Foreground service use must satisfy the foreground service criteria of the Device and Network Abuse policy, including being perceptible to the user through a user-initiated action or a clear, accurate ongoing notification.

Apps targeting Android 14+ must declare each foreground service type on the Play Console App content page with a description of the feature, the user impact if the system defers or interrupts the task, a link to a video showing how the user triggers it, and the chosen use case.

Each foreground service type declaration must link to a video that should show the in-app steps a user takes to trigger the feature, and the video must show a user-initiated action rather than automatic background work, in-app setup rather than system settings for connected devices, and user-started playback rather than automatic soundtracks for media playback.

Foreground service types must best match the actual use (the help page gives a non-exhaustive mapping, for example user-initiated work for dataSync and user-started playback for mediaPlayback, and unlisted use cases can be entered manually), and TYPE_SPECIAL_USE may be declared only when no defined type fits and the other foreground service criteria are met.
Apps that use USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT must complete the Play Console full-screen intent declaration stating whether their core functionality qualifies for automatic granting.

For apps targeting Android 14+, USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is enabled by default only for apps whose core function is alarms or receiving phone or video calls and whose Play Console declaration was approved; apps without a completed or approved declaration must prompt users to grant it on new installs and degrade gracefully if it is denied.

title: App testing requirements for new personal developer accounts
requirements: Apps from personal developer accounts created after November 13, 2023 must pass a closed test before production: at least 12 testers opted in continuously for the 14 days immediately before applying, where testers who opt out or test for fewer than 14 consecutive days do not count.
App setup in Play Console must be complete before a closed test can start.

Such accounts must apply for production access from the Play Console Dashboard, answering questions about the closed test (tester recruitment and engagement, a summary of feedback and how it was collected), the app (target audience, value proposition, expected first-year installs), and production readiness (changes made from testing and how readiness was judged).

Production, pre-registration and open testing stay unavailable to such accounts until production access is granted, and too few opted-in testers or weak tester engagement can require continued testing.

Before applying for production access, the app's content, features and monetization must comply with Play policies, its target age group and listing settings must match its audience and content, it must be stable without crashes, broken features or missing screens, and apps requiring sign-in must have valid working test credentials in Play Console.

title: Device verification requirements for new developer accounts
requirements: New personal developer accounts must verify, as the account owner through the Play Console mobile app, that they have access to a real non-rooted physical Android device running Android 10 or later before they can make apps available on Google Play.

title: Prepare and roll out a release
requirements: Releases must be uploaded as Android App Bundles; APKs are accepted only for legacy apps created before August 2021.

The first release of an app must configure Play App Signing; the signing key may be changed only during the first release (which cuts off existing internal and closed testers from updates and requires re-uploading versions) and becomes fixed once the app is published to an open track.
Personal accounts created after November 13, 2023 must meet the personal account testing requirements before releasing to production.

A new release cannot be created while outstanding releases exist; staged releases must be rolled out to 100% or unpublished releases discarded first, and outstanding Dashboard setup tasks must be completed if Create new release is disabled.
The account member creating a release must hold the Release apps to testing tracks permission.
Apps whose bundles request high-risk or sensitive permissions (for example SMS or Call Log) may need to file the Permissions Declaration Form and obtain Google Play approval.
Release notes (What's new) must describe the changes in the release, must not be promotional or solicit user actions, and are limited to 500 Unicode characters per supported language.
All errors in the Errors summary on the Preview and confirm screen must be resolved before the release can be published.

A first production rollout has no staged percentage and publishes the app to all users in the countries and regions selected for the track, so country and region targeting must be set correctly before rollout.

title: Prepare your app for review
requirements: All App content declarations, including those under Needs attention, must be completed before their deadlines and kept up to date.
Every app must link a privacy policy both in its store listing and inside the app, even if it accesses no personal or sensitive data and does not target children.

The privacy policy must be on an active, publicly accessible http or https URL with a valid SSL certificate, reachable worldwide without geofencing or login, shown as a standard non-editable webpage (not a PDF or download), specific to the app, and must fully disclose how the app collects, uses and shares user data, including the types of parties it is shared with.

The Contains ads declaration must be accurate: answer Yes for ads from third-party ad SDKs, banners, interstitials, native or sponsored in-feed ads and house ads promoting the developer's other apps; a More Apps style menu entry that does not interfere with or embed in gameplay does not count as ads.
Paid product placements in the app must comply with local laws.

Apps restricted in whole or part by login, membership, location or other authentication must provide sign-in details that give reviewers full access, noting special mechanisms such as one-time passwords, multi-factor authentication or logins with more than two fields.
The target age group must be declared accurately in Target audience and content, and apps that include children in the target audience must comply with the Families policy.
Apps requesting high-risk or sensitive permissions such as SMS or Call Log may need to file the Permissions Declaration Form and receive approval.
The content rating questionnaire must be completed for each app so it is not listed as Unrated, since unrated apps may be removed.
The app's privacy and security practices must be declared in the Data safety section.
